headline: A wave of critical patches from Zoom, Splunk, and F5 lands alongside a Secure Boot bypass hiding in forgotten bootloaders, while Russian-speaking crews trojanize video apps to steal credentials and crypto.

emerging_trends.text: Russian-speaking crews keep burying malware inside the software people already trust, lacing WebEx and Zoom installers with the Starland RAT to lift credentials and cryptocurrency from victims across the United States and Europe.
emerging_trends.topic_title: UAT-11795 Starland RAT via Trojanized Video Apps

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep finding purchase beneath the operating system, where nearly a dozen revoked UEFI shim bootloaders stayed trusted for years and hand any machine a clean Secure Boot bypass.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Forgotten UEFI Shims Bypass Secure Boot

emerging_trends.text: The offense-defense contest inside AI sped up as OpenAI unveiled GPT-Red, an automated red-teamer built to break its own models before customers can, even as researchers insist a human must still prove any bug the machine flags.

topics.title: Critical Zoom, Splunk, and F5 Flaws Patched
topics.latest_developments: Zoom shipped fixes for CVE-2026-53412, a 9.8-severity improper-input-validation flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker take over Windows accounts, a day after warning of it, while Splunk and F5 patched critical bugs of their own across their platforms and the NGINX and BIG-IP lines.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-53412 affects the Zoom Desktop, VDI, and Meeting SDK clients for Windows; Splunk's flaws expose credentials and enable privilege escalation, and F5's NGINX and BIG-IP bugs allow configuration changes, memory leaks, and code execution. Apply every vendor update now.

sources.title: Zoom Patches Critical Windows Flaw That Could Enable Account Takeover
Splunk, Zoom Patch Critical Vulnerabilities
F5 Patches Multiple NGINX, BIG-IP Vulnerabilities
Zoom warns of critical account takeover vulnerability

topics.title: Breaches Hit 23andMe, Nichirei Logistics, and Romania's Land Registry
topics.latest_developments: 23andMe agreed to pay $18 million to settle claims from 43 state attorneys general over its failure to protect genetic data, as fresh attacks knocked out Japan's largest cold-chain operator Nichirei Logistics Group—short-supplying KFC restaurants and supermarkets—and Romania's national cadastre agency ANCPI, whose e-Terra land registry went dark with data now allegedly for sale.
topics.summary: The 23andMe settlement resolves fallout from its earlier customer-data breach, while the Nichirei and ANCPI incidents show cyberattacks halting food logistics and government land records in real time. Expect regulatory and operational pressure on data custodians.

sources.title: 23andMe to pay $18 million in new genetics data breach settlement
Cyberattack on Japan's largest cold-chain operator disrupts KFC, supermarket supplies
Romania's land registry hit by cyber attack, data allegedly for sale

topics.title: Forgotten UEFI Shims Bypass Secure Boot
topics.latest_developments: Researchers found nearly a dozen old UEFI shim bootloaders, each carrying a valid Microsoft signature and only recently revoked, that stayed trusted for years and let an attacker bypass Secure Boot on any machine regardless of its operating system.
topics.summary: Shims chain-load an OS bootloader after Secure Boot verifies them, and because the vulnerable versions kept valid Microsoft signatures, an attacker who plants one can load unsigned code before the operating system starts. Update the shim revocation list and firmware.

sources.title: Old UEFI Shims Expose Systems to Secure Boot Bypass
Forgotten Bootloaders Expose Secure Boot Blind Spot

topics.title: UAT-11795 Starland RAT via Trojanized Video Apps
topics.latest_developments: Cisco Talos and BleepingComputer detailed UAT-11795, a Russian-speaking, financially motivated actor active since at least June 2025 that trojanizes WebEx and Zoom installers to drop the novel Starland RAT and a bespoke WLDR command-and-control implant.
topics.summary: The campaign steals credentials and cryptocurrency from targets across the United States and Europe. Download conferencing software only from vendor sites and verify installer signatures.

sources.title: Russian hackers trojanize WebEx, Zoom apps to push Starland malware
UAT-11795 deploys novel Starland RAT and bespoke WLDR C2 implant in financially motivated campaign

topics.title: Sandworm Fake-CAPTCHA PowerShell Attacks
topics.latest_developments: Ukraine's responders caught Sandworm, Russia's GRU-linked group, replacing a website CAPTCHA with instructions telling Ukrainian visitors to paste a PowerShell command into Windows, the same copy-paste ClickFix trick that criminal operators use to spread the new modular TELEPUZ malware documented by Elastic Security Labs.
topics.summary: ClickFix lures dress malware execution as a routine human-verification step, sidestepping downloads and many defenses. Train users never to paste commands from a web page into a terminal.

sources.title: Sandworm hackers have a CAPTCHA trick for Ukrainians
New TELEPUZ Malware Spreads via ClickFix to Steal Data and Run Commands

topics.title: OpenAI Debuts GPT-Red Automated Red-Teamer
topics.latest_developments: OpenAI disclosed GPT-Red, an internal automated red-teaming model it uses to discover prompt-injection weaknesses at scale and adversarially train its GPT-5.6 Sol release, landing as researchers argue AI can surface bugs quickly but a human still has to prove each one real.
topics.summary: GPT-Red generates prompt-injection attacks against OpenAI's own models to fix flaws before wide deployment. The push reflects a broader shift toward automated offense balanced by human verification of findings.

sources.title: OpenAI's GPT-Red Automates Prompt Injection Testing to Harden GPT-5.6 Sol
AI Can Find Bugs, But Human Knowledge Still Proves Them

business_politics.title: U.S.-Iran War Grinds On as Hormuz Stays Choked
business_politics.latest_developments: The U.S. military expanded its strikes into northern Iran and disabled a ship trying to run the blockade, Iran released American woman Dena Karari after more than a year in detention as what Trump called a goodwill gesture, and oil rose for a fourth straight session as Strait of Hormuz transit thinned to a trickle.
business_politics.summary: The renewed U.S. campaign against Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed, squeezing the world's main oil artery; crude climbed a fourth day and gold briefly slipped below $4,000 as traders weighed Tehran's threat to halt energy exports against Washington's threat to strike Iranian civilian infrastructure.

sources.title: Oil Futures Make Moderate Gains Awaiting U.S.-Iran Moves
Iran Allows U.S. Citizen It Held for More Than a Year to Leave

business.title: Schwebel's Buyer Talks Collapse
business.latest_developments: Talks with a potential buyer for Schwebel Baking Company have come to a close, the Post-Gazette reported July 16, dimming the prospects for the bread maker.
business.summary: Schwebel Baking Company, a longtime regional bread and roll maker, ended negotiations with a would-be purchaser, leaving the company's future and its workforce in doubt.

sources.title: Talks with potential buyer for Schwebel's have 'come to a close'

business.title: PJM Auction Hits Price Cap Again
business.latest_developments: PJM Interconnection's latest capacity auction cleared at the price cap for a second straight year, and CEO David Mills said demand keeps growing faster than supply, pointing to higher electricity bills across Pennsylvania.
business.summary: PJM Interconnection, the grid operator serving Pennsylvania and 12 other states, again saw its capacity auction hit the maximum allowed price, a result consumer advocates warn will push electricity rates up for households across the region.

sources.title: Regional electricity price hits cap again in latest auction

business.title: WVU, Pitt, CMU Land Energy Hub
business.latest_developments: West Virginia University won $160 million in new federal money from the National Science Foundation's RETI Engine and will partner with the University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Mellon University to build an industrial energy innovation hub.
business.summary: The National Science Foundation grant ties WVU, Pitt, and Carnegie Mellon together to develop industrial energy technology, one of the larger research awards flowing to the Pittsburgh region's universities.

sources.title: With $160 million in new government funding, WVU partners with Pitt and CMU to develop industrial energy innovation hub

around_town.title: Allegheny County Pension Shortfall Hits $1.4 Billion
around_town.latest_developments: A new report from Allegheny County Treasurer Erica Rocchi Brussalars, out July 16, pegs the county's pension shortfall at $1.4 billion and says the county must find an extra $100 million a year for 20 years to fix it.
around_town.summary: Allegheny County's underfunded pension system, long left to fester, has come due, and closing the gap will demand roughly $100 million in new money annually for two decades under Executive Sara Innamorato, a strain the county has yet to fund.

sources.title: New report highlights Allegheny County's pension fund crisis
Brandon McGinley: How Pittsburgh escaped pension hell, and the lessons for Allegheny County

events.title: LÚNASA Celtic Festival Coming to Arts Landing
events.latest_developments: The Irish Partnership of Pittsburgh and Anam Arts announced LÚNASA: A Celtic Festival Cultivating the Light of Belonging, a new event coming to Arts Landing in Downtown Pittsburgh later this summer.
events.summary: LÚNASA is a new Celtic-heritage festival from the Irish Partnership of Pittsburgh, which also runs the annual Pittsburgh Irish Festival, staged at Arts Landing Downtown as a first-year cultural tradition.

sources.title: A New Celebration of Celtic Heritage Is Coming to Arts Landing

around_teams.title: Ramsey as Graham's Chess Piece
around_teams.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette training-camp countdown argues cornerback Jalen Ramsey must be defensive coordinator Patrick Graham's ultimate movable chess piece as the Steelers open camp at Saint Vincent College in Latrobe.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette frames Ramsey, the veteran cornerback the Steelers acquired for their secondary, as the versatile defender Graham can line up all over the field, a linchpin of Pittsburgh's 2026 defense.

sources.title: Steelers training camp countdown: Jalen Ramsey must be Patrick Graham's ultimate chess piece

team_usa.title: Flavor Flav Backs Team USA Women's Hockey
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN detailed July 15 how rapper Flavor Flav became the driving force behind the inaugural SHE Weekend in Las Vegas, his biggest show of support yet for the U.S. women's national ice hockey team.
team_usa.summary: Flavor Flav, an unexpected champion of women's sports, is bankrolling and headlining SHE Weekend, an event built around Team USA women's ice hockey players as they push their sport toward a bigger stage.

sources.title: How (and why) did Flavor Flav become the driving force behind SHE Weekend?
